Hi Ben,

We're getting ready to onboard Redwood's private deployment into our SIEM. We need a clear mapping of the log and trace fields you export from the on-prem forwarder and the recommended transport modes (HEC, S3 push, or Kafka). Specifically: 

- Field-level mapping to our Splunk schema (timestamp, host, service, span_id, trace_id, user_id, request_path, response_code, model_id, request_tokens, response_tokens)
- Delivery guarantees (TLS, auth, retries, at-least-once/at-most-once)

Can you send a short plan and a mapping artifact we can review? Our timeline is 2 weeks — we want to validate the mapping and run a test-forwarder into a staging index.

Ben / Elena — attaching our first-pass artifacts. Below is a concise technical plan and decisions for the on-prem observability handoff.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_forwarder_spec.pdf, obsv-field-mapping-catalog.csv, acme_siem_mapping_draft.xlsx

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- We can export logs, metrics and traces from the private deployment using our lightweight forwarder. Supported sinks: Splunk HEC (HTTP Event Collector), S3 (encrypted, signed), Kafka (TLS + SASL).
- Default delivery model: TLS + token auth to HEC for low-latency; S3 as a fallback/archival path. We support configurable at-least-once delivery with duplicate suppression via event dedupe IDs.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry-compatible spans emitted from the runtime; trace_id/span_id fields map directly to your span index.

Field-level notes (highlights from the attached CSV)
- redwood.timestamp -> _time (epoch ms)
- redwood.host_id -> host
- redwood.service -> service
- redwood.trace.trace_id -> trace_id
- redwood.trace.span_id -> span_id
- redwood.user.id (opt-in) -> user_id (REDACTABLE)
- redwood.request.path -> request_path
- redwood.response.code -> response_code
- redwood.model.name -> model_id
- redwood.metrics.request_tokens -> request_tokens
- redwood.metrics.response_tokens -> response_tokens

PII / sensitive data handling
- user identifiers and prompt text are flagged as optional PII. We provide a pre-forward redaction hook and a hashing option (sha256) for user ids. Prompt text can be redacted or persisted to your archival S3 with separate ACLs.

Operational controls and rollout
- Canary: start with metadata-only (no prompt text) -> enable full logs after 48h validation.
- Rate limits: forwarder supports batch-size and max-requests-per-second config so we can stay within your ingestion quota.
- Backpressure: forwarder will queue to disk and retry with exponential backoff; we expose metrics for queue length and retry_count.

Test plan (staging)
- Week 1: field mapping alignment and HEC ingestion smoke test (10k events).
- Week 2: canary with production-like traffic (sampled prompts, metrics, and traces) into a dedicated staging index.

Open questions for Acme:
- Which Splunk index / HEC token will we use for staging?
- Retention target for logs (days) and traces (days) — we'll mirror retention knobs in forwarder config and document retention on your side.

I'll follow up with a short-runbook for the forwarder install and a sample docker-compose for the onprem case.

— Marissa
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
